section.budget.title: Tool budgets
section.budget.subtitle: Time limits, output caps and read line counts for the built-in tools
field.bashTimeoutMs.label: Default command timeout (ms)
field.bashTimeoutMs.help: bash closes the process tree after this long when the call has no timeoutMs argument. If the model passes timeoutMs, its value is used but still capped by the limit below.
field.bashMaxTimeoutMs.label: Command timeout ceiling (ms)
field.bashMaxTimeoutMs.help: The model cannot go past this: longer work should be split up. Before raising it, ask yourself whether you want one turn to hang that long.
field.bashOutputChars.label: Command output cap (characters)
field.bashOutputChars.help: Anything longer is truncated with a note. With the spill plugin on, big output goes to disk past its threshold and only the head and tail come back; this cap is the fallback when that plugin is off.
field.readLineLimit.label: Default lines per read
field.readLineLimit.help: How many lines read returns at a time; for longer files the model can continue with offset/limit.
save.unknownKey: This section has no such setting: {key}
section.shell.title: Terminal environment
section.shell.subtitle: Which shells on this machine can run commands, and which one the bash tool uses by default
field.bashShell.label: Default terminal
field.bashShell.help: The bash tool and terminal sessions both start processes from here. Switching also changes the tool description the model sees, so it writes commands in the new terminal's syntax. Only shells actually detected on this machine are listed.
field.bashShell.option.missing: {shell} (not available now; falls back to the platform default)
field.detected.label: Detected
field.redetect.label: Detect again
field.redetect.help: Click after installing PowerShell 7 / Git / WSL; no restart needed.
save.shellMissing: {shell} was not detected on this machine; install it first (or click “Detect again”).
save.shellSwitched: Switched to {shell}; it takes effect from the next command.
